subject: Request: Multizone mixed-degradation apportionment and maintenance exception
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: support@valence.net
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partial latency spikes on API path — multizone overlap

Hi Valence team,

Thanks for the initial incident summary, Ari. Clearview is pushing back because the way our monthly uptime ledger rolled up multiple short-duration degradations pushed the April SLO below 99.95% for one customer route. They believe a portion of the degraded minutes should be excluded as scheduled maintenance in Valence's edge fabric (you list a maintenance window on 2027-04-16 03:00-04:00 UTC, but our traceroutes show the larger latency tail persisted across two AZs until 03:27 UTC).

We need two things to assess apportionment:
- An explicit mapping from Valence maintenance CIDR/POP list -> the probe vantage points that would be impacted.
- Per-pop/zone telemetry showing when the fabric returned to nominal (1-min resolution is OK).

If Valence confirms the degradation in one POP caused cascades into other POPs (i.e., routing shifts), we need that evidence so we can mark the portion attributable to their maintenance. If not, we will treat the full window as Redwood service degradation and escalate a credit request from Clearview.

Attaching our consolidated probe logs and the workbook with the ledger that produced the April tally. Please respond by EOD Monday 2027-04-19 so we can update Clearview's billing/CS thread.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

Attachments: uptime_calc_multizone.xlsx (spreadsheet), synthetic_probe_logs_20270415-17.txt (text log)
From: Ari Kaplan <ari@valence.net>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, support@valence.net
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 12:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partial latency spikes on API path — multizone overlap

Hi Jonas —

Appreciate the data. Quick summary from Valence Ops: we had an automated certificate rotation job that hit a control-plane race in POP-7 (us-west-2 equivalent) between 03:01–03:12 UTC; that POP did return to nominal at 03:12. The 03:12–03:27 tail you see is consistent with our BGP flap mitigation where traffic was re-homed to POP-3 and POP-5 while we rebuilt sessions.

I've attached the POP logs and a short incident report. Two notes:
1) Our maintenance window was scheduled and announced; per our terms, scheduled maintenance for control plane changes is listed as an exception if it appears in our maintenance registry.
2) We do not automatically exclude downstream routing flaps that occur due to re-homing unless the root cause is strictly within our control-plane change. We can provide session-level evidence showing the chain (control-plane rotate -> session rebuild -> BGP dampening) which would support partial attribution.

I will push the session evidence by Monday morning. If you can highlight the exact minutes Redwood attributes to customer-facing errors (you already flagged 03:02–03:27 UTC in your workbook), that will speed the apportionment.

—Ari
Ari Kaplan
Valence CDN — Technical Ops

Attachments: valence_incident_report_20270416.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Re: Partial latency spikes on API path — multizone overlap

Forwarding Ari's note and the partial evidence. Jonas — I took a quick pass through the ledger and there are three separate short spikes across the month that, when summed, pushed Clearview under the SLA threshold. Clearview's CS wants a clear apportionment so we can either:

- Request a proportional credit for the minutes we still own, or
- If Valence accepts full attribution for the merged window, request a full month adjustment.

Ben, can you run the ledger with and without the Valence-excluded minutes once Ari provides the session dump? I'm worried about our policy of counting contiguous degraded minutes even if the root cause shifts mid-window — it biases against customers during multizone maintenance.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari@valence.net>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Partial latency spikes on API path — multizone overlap

Ari / Valence team —

Received the incident report. I pulled the ledger and ran a sensitivity check: if we exclude the period 03:01–03:12 UTC as Valence maintenance, Clearview still crosses the SLA boundary because of an independent 03:18–03:27 tail where our probes see >250ms p95 across two AZs. That span appears to correlate with BGP re-homing but it's not explicit in the Valence report yet.

Two asks so we can close this swiftly:
1) Per-pop session dumps for 03:00–03:30 UTC (Hash/flow ids) to show whether the 03:18–03:27 tail was solely a routing artifact or an application-level queueing event on our side.
2) Confirmation of whether Valence classifies BGP re-homing tails that follow a scheduled control-plane change as maintenance-excludable under your published uptime exceptions.

If Valence accepts the routing tail as excludable, our ledger will drop below the credit threshold and we can provide a partial apportionment credit to Clearview; otherwise we return to the customer asking for proactive mitigation and propose a goodwill credit from Redwood for the minutes we accept.

Ben Carter
Program Lead, Reliability Escalations — Redwood Inference
From: Ari Kaplan <ari@valence.net>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 07:33:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Partial latency spikes on API path — multizone overlap

Ben —

I've attached session dumps per-pop and a short annotation mapping the BGP state changes. We classify the routing tail that results directly from our control-plane rotate as maintenance-related for the purpose of uptime apportionment (see clause 4.b in our Ops exceptions), but we explicitly exclude sequelae once traffic reaches a non-Valence transit hop and the downstream provider shows queuing.

In the files I'm sending: POP-7 control-plane rotate clears at 03:12; session rebuilds finish at 03:14; re-homing completes 03:17; POP-3 shows sustained elevated retransmits 03:18–03:26 which is outside our ridge. Based on that, Valence accepts apportionment for 03:01–03:17 but not 03:18–03:27.

If Redwood's ledger excludes 03:01–03:17, please share the revised tally and we'll confirm on our side.

—Ari
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari@valence.net>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Partial latency spikes on API path — multizone overlap

Ari — thanks for the quick turnaround and the per-pop dumps. I ran the ledger with Valence's accepted exclusion (03:01–03:17 UTC) and the updated result still leaves Clearview 0.02% short of their monthly 99.95% SLO because of the 03:18–03:27 window plus two other unrelated 2–3 minute spikes earlier in April on an independent path.

Proposal to resolve:
- Redwood will accept Valence's apportionment for 03:01–03:17 (we will exclude those minutes).
- For the remaining minutes, Redwood proposes a one-off goodwill credit equal to 20% of the proportional monthly invoice for Clearview while we complete a root-cause follow-up with the downstream transit provider. This keeps the customer whole while we finish the postmortem.

Marissa — please approve the goodwill credit and coordinate with Billing. Ben — open a follow-up ticket to trace the 03:18–03:27 tail with the downstream transit provider and assign priority P2.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: revised_ledger_excluding_valence_minutes.csv
